 RAHUL TALJABHAI RABARI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT =======================================================
Appearance:
MR PR ABICHANDANI with MS POONAM M MAHETA(11265) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR ANVESH V VYAS(5654) for the Respondent(s) No. 1 MR DHAWAN JAYSWAL APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 =======================================================

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of rule for respondent - State of Gujarat.

2. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11217041230159/2023 registered with the Saraswati Police Station, Patan for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471,
409, 120(B) and 201 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the so-called incident has taken place for the period between 01.01.2019 to 23.06.2021, for which, the FIR has been lodged on 15.04.2023 and the applicant has been arrested in connection with the same on 10.12.2023 and since then, he is in judicial custody.

Learned advocate submitted that now the investigation is completed and after NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5408/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined submission of the chargesheet, the present application is preferred.
Learned advocate submitted that there is inordinate and unexplained delay caused in filing aforesaid FIR.
Learned advocate submitted that FIR has been filed against total 15 accused persons, wherein the applicant is shown as accused no.14.

Learned advocate submitted that it is the case of the prosecution that all the accused have Rahul Taljabhai Rabari vs State Of Gujarat on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101229444/
1 made hand-in-glow with each other and with a sole intent to defraud the bank, they have created false and fabricated documents and produced before the bank and on the strength of the said documents, they have obtained loan in the name of the dead persons as well as in the name of the persons, who are in fact not the owner of the property and by doing so, they have misappropriated huge volume of money of the bank.

sentences.text: Learned advocate submitted that it is the case of the prosecution that at the relevant point of time, the present applicant was working as Secretary of the bank but in fact, the present applicant was the Member of the society and he had taken over the charge of Secretary w.e.f. 01.04.2023, therefore, he had worked as Secretary for very less period i.e. only for three months.
Learned advocate submitted that other co-accused, whose role is similar or graver have already been considered by this Court.
Learned advocate submitted that all the offences are exclusively triable by the Court of Magistrate.

undefined advocate submitted that entire case of the prosecution hinges upon documentary evidence, which have been collected by the IO during the course of investigation and number of witnesses have been cited in the chargesheet and, hence, trial would get delayed.

Learned advocate, under the instructions, submitted that without prejudice to his rights and contentions, the applicant is ready and willing to deposit Rs.6,00,000/- before the concerned trial court, out of which, the applicant will deposit Rs.50,000/- within ten days from the date of his release and remaining amount of Rs.5,50,000/- will be deposited in eleven equal installments thereafter i.e. on or before 30the day of each month beginning from June, 2024 and in support of it,
the father of the applicant has filed an affidavit narrating the above facts and after the release, the applicant will also file such undertaking.
It is, therefore, urged that considering the nature of the offence and on the ground of parity, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
4. Learned APP, Mr. Dabhi for the respondent-State as well learned advocate, Mr. Vyas for original complainant have opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
It is submitted that the role of the present applicant is clearly spelt out from the papers of the chargesheet.
Learned advocates submitted that the present applicant is the kingpin and he is the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5408/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined main instrumental to dupe the bank.
Learned advocates submitted that the present applicant was working as Secretary and during his tenure, the alleged incident has taken place.

Learned advocates submitted that for the purpose of obtaining loan from the bank, all the accused have connived and made hand-in-glow with each other and as a part of conspiracy, they have acted in a particular manner and they have prepared false and fabricated documents, produced it before the bank and on the strength of those documents, they have obtained loan from the bank and by doing so, they have duped the bank.
Learned advocates, therefore, urged that considering the gravity and seriousness of the offence the present application may not be entertained.
5. Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

6. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.

It is found out from the record that the present application is preferred after Rahul Taljabhai Rabari vs State Of Gujarat on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101229444/
2 submission of the chargesheet and now the investigation is completed and the applicant is in jail since 10.12.2023.

sentences.text: All the offences are exclusively triable by the Court of Magistrate.

The case of the prosecution hinges NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5408/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined upon documentary evidence, which have been collected by the IO during the course of investigation and number of witnesses have been cited as witness in the chargesheet papers and because of which, trial will take considerable time to conclude.
I have considered the role attributed to the present applicant at the time of commission of crime and the role of the co- accused, who has been considered by this Court.
Further as stated above, willingness has been shown by the applicant to deposit Rs.6,00,000/- before the concerned court without prejudice to his rights and contentions.
Therefore considering the above factual aspects and on the ground of parity, the present application deserves to be allowed.

7. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40 as well as in case of Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51.
